answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded registry. Every operator posts a stake at registration, slashed entirely if the identity is proven a duplicate. Dedup keys on settled-work history, not claims, so a canyon of fresh clones sits empty beside a real operator. A farm must post the whole bond per fake identity and feed each one real work per epoch, or forfeit it. Honest accounts pay one bond; each fake pays the same and earns nothing, so cost scales per identity while reward stays flat. The settled-work signal makes the hollow drawer of clones cost more than it returns.
